source_evidence.note: Evidence supports partial instructional depth, not missing canonical concepts or verified jurisdiction coverage.

enrichments.concept: Construct and interpret complete five-bin histograms and compare distributions
enrichments.grades: Grades 6–8 provisional; do not assert Maryland Grade 7 placement
enrichments.scope: 20 bounded whole-number observations in bins [0,5),[5,10),[10,15),[15,20),[20,25). Count each observation exactly once, compare modal bin and grouped frequencies.
prerequisites: Count frequency and distinguish observation from frequency

diagnostic.prompt: Where does a score of exactly 10 belong: 5–9 or 10–14?
Five bars have counts 2,3,4,1,0. How many observations?

worked_examples.concrete: Sort ten score cards and place each in a labeled basket.
Place cards on interval boundary labels.
worked_examples.visual: Each boundary starts its own new bin.

worked_examples.prompt: A scores 1,2,7,11,16,17,22,24; B scores 0,6,10,14,18,20,21,9. Which has more scores at least 15?
worked_examples.concrete: Group score cards at 15 and above.
worked_examples.visual: Add last two bar heights for each class.

misconception_pathways.wrong_idea: An interval includes both its endpoints
hints: Write the intervals as whole-number ranges.
misconception_pathways.repair: Highlight left-closed/right-open bin boundaries and move a boundary card.

misconception_pathways.wrong_idea: Bar height represents score magnitude, not frequency
misconception_pathways.probe: If 20–24 has one observation, should its bar reach 24?
hints: What does the vertical axis count?
How many observations lie in that bin?
Separate bin label from bar height.
misconception_pathways.repair: Build a tally table beside the histogram.

misconception_pathways.wrong_idea: Empty bins can be omitted and bar widths changed
misconception_pathways.probe: Should 15–19 disappear when no score occurs there?
hints: What does the horizontal scale represent?
Would removing a bin shift the next interval?
misconception_pathways.repair: Retain all equal-width intervals with an explicit zero frequency.

enrichments.socratic_hint_policy: Three progressive prompts during guided practice; no hints in independent assessment.

guided_practice.scaffold: Move five cards to labeled bins.

guided_practice.prompt: Which bin is modal if counts are 2,4,7,5,2?
Class A has 4 scores in 15–19 and 3 in 20–24; B has 2 and 4. Who has more at least 15?
guided_practice.scaffold: Combine two last-bin counts per class.

independent_assessment.oracle: Frequencies 3,2,4,0,1; unique max at third interval.

independent_assessment.prompt: A scores 15,16,20,21,0; B scores 15,20,0,1,2. Which class has more scores 15–24?

mve_spec.scene: Five adjacent fixed-width bins, raw-data table and tally table
guided_interactions: Keyboard move each observation into one bin
Toggle count conservation without revealing target until submitted
Compare two histograms on same scale
accessibility: Announce interval inclusivity and bar count
Provide sortable data table and textual bar description
mve_spec.independent: No auto-filled bins, bar heights, counts or hints before final submission.

enrichments.concept: Recognize valid and invalid six-square cube nets and reason about exact face area
enrichments.grades: Grades 6–8 provisional; current Maryland placement requires mapping review
enrichments.scope: Six connected congruent squares on a unit grid; 35 free hexominoes partition into 11 cube nets and 24 non-nets; exact rational edge surface area.
prerequisites: Identify shared edges and distinguish overlap

diagnostic.prompt: Does a straight line of six squares form a cube net?
How many distinct outward faces must a valid net cover?

worked_examples.concrete: Cut and hinge six square cards.
worked_examples.visual: Fold the central strip and close two remaining faces.
worked_examples.symbolic: Six distinct face normals after 90-degree folds.

worked_examples.prompt: Can six squares in a straight row fold into a cube?
worked_examples.concrete: Hinge six squares in a chain.
worked_examples.visual: After four side faces, later faces overlap rather than cap opposite ends.
worked_examples.symbolic: Repeated outward face normals; fewer than six unique faces.

worked_examples.prompt: Can a 2-by-3 solid rectangle of six squares fold into a cube?
worked_examples.visual: A folding cycle forces inconsistent orientation or overlap.
worked_examples.symbolic: Cannot assign six consistent distinct outward normals.

worked_examples.concrete: Lay out the six squares as a zigzag strip.
worked_examples.visual: Trace each right-angle hinge and mark distinct cube faces.
worked_examples.symbolic: Six outward normals are unique and consistent.

worked_examples.prompt: A cube net has square edge 3/2 cm. Find its total face area.
worked_examples.concrete: Cover each face with a square of side 3/2 cm.
worked_examples.visual: Six faces each have area 9/4 cm².

misconception_pathways.wrong_idea: Any six connected squares are a valid net
hints: How many cube faces must be distinct?
What happens around a cycle of four adjacent squares?
misconception_pathways.repair: Track repeated face directions and collisions.

misconception_pathways.wrong_idea: Rotation or reflection changes whether a net folds
misconception_pathways.probe: If a valid net is rotated on paper, does it stop being valid?
hints: Do the same hinge relations remain?
Compare folded faces after turning the page.
misconception_pathways.repair: Rotate/reflect a shape and preserve face identity.

misconception_pathways.wrong_idea: Surface area is six times edge length
misconception_pathways.probe: For edge 3/2 cm, is surface area 9 cm²?
hints: What is the area of one square face?
Square the edge length before multiplying.
misconception_pathways.repair: Overlay six face-area tiles and annotate cm².

enrichments.socratic_hint_policy: Guided-only three progressive prompts; independent foldability checks never expose collision or orientation hints.

guided_practice.prompt: Are six collinear squares a cube net?
How many distinct face directions does a valid cube net produce?
Cube edge 1/2 m: total surface area?
Does rotating a valid cube net 90 degrees change its foldability?

independent_assessment.oracle: Six unique face normals under hinge rotations.

independent_assessment.prompt: Can a 2-by-3 rectangle of squares fold into a cube without overlap?
independent_assessment.oracle: Inconsistent face orientations in closed grid cycles.

independent_assessment.prompt: A valid cube net has edge 2/3 cm. Find total surface area.

mve_spec.scene: 2D six-square grid with optional 3D fold preview (content specification only)
guided_interactions: Keyboard select hinge and rotate 90 degrees
Show collisions and six face normals only in guided mode
Rotate and reflect entire net preserving connectivity
Tile faces to visualize rational square area
accessibility: Describe coordinates and adjacency in text
Provide keyboard-only hinge sequence and static folding transcript
Do not rely on color or 3D-only cues
mve_spec.independent: No 3D fold preview, collisions, normal indicators or area tiles until after submission.
